A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching title, authors, and central research questions. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and rendered figures support comparison despite extensive reorganization and substantive revisions.

before.justification: v2 reports original OpenML and synthetic-data experiments comparing objectives, tuning methods, optimal versus greedy trees, noise sensitivity, and runtime, including additional appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 reports original revised benchmark and simulation results, including additional experiments with original numerical features and balanced accuracy in Appendices D–E.

M1.justification: v3 removes the proposed M-loss and L-loss adaptations and question-length penalization introduced in v2 Sections 3.3 and 4.1. This substantially narrows the proposed method repertoire. Laplace smoothing and the core STreeD/CART procedures remain; the new pseudocode explains existing algorithms.

E1.justification: The OpenML benchmark changes from 180 to 109 datasets. Matching the appendix lists establishes removal of 75 datasets below 250 instances and bank-marketing, alongside six additions including credit-g, Bank_Customer_Churn, and E-CommereShippingData. Covertype, Higgs, and the synthetic tree and linear-separator families remain.

E2.justification: The corresponding objective comparisons shrink from eleven objectives to seven, removing square-root Gini, MDL-Mehta, M-loss, and L-loss. M-loss also disappears from the accuracy–size comparison, and question-length tuning disappears from the tuning comparison. These are substantive changes to evaluated comparator membership.

E3.justification: The main tuning budget changes from k=16 to k=10, tuning is uniformly described as five-fold, and matched CART–ODT accuracy comparisons extend to depth five. Inverse-size-weighted SWA is replaced by uniformly weighted SE-AUC. New appendix protocols evaluate unbinarized features using ConTree with a 24-hour limit and balanced accuracy using class weighting.

E4.justification: Appendices D–E add checks of whether conclusions persist without binarization and under a balanced-accuracy objective. v3 removes v2’s objective-specific and tuning-specific noise analyses, ground-truth complexity experiment, question-length study, training/test learning curves, and binarization-granularity sensitivity analysis. These substantially change the questions investigated beyond the main comparisons.

E5.justification: The synthetic comparisons described in v2 Section 5.4.1 report 500 repetitions, versus 1000 in v3. v3 newly specifies averaging fold ranks within datasets before Nemenyi testing; this disclosure does not establish how v2 implemented the test. Nemenyi testing remains, while the explicit objective-noise confidence intervals and small-dataset standard-error summaries are removed.

E6.justification: v2 Figure 11 reports depth-four ODT/CART accuracies of 80.2%/79.2% on 180 datasets; v3 Figure 5 reports 81.0%/79.4% on 109 and adds depth-five results of 82.2%/80.5%. These are revised benchmark summaries, not same-setting gains. New appendix results include nonsignificant numerical-feature comparisons and mixed balanced-accuracy rankings, while numerous earlier diagnostic results disappear.

T1.justification: The inverse-size-weighted accuracy definition in v2 Equation 1 becomes uniform average error in v3 Definition 1, changing the mathematical quantity measured. v3 also corrects the stated Bayesian leaf objective from a Beta-function ratio to its negative logarithm and removes the novel-loss formulas and objective counterexamples from v2.

C1.justification: v3 drops v2’s claimed contributions of new losses and tuning approaches, together with its conclusions about increasing concept complexity and near-equal question lengths. It emphasizes direct target-objective optimization and the accuracy–size trade-off, replaces SWA with SE-AUC, and strengthens the headline noise conclusion from no greater overfitting to lower noise sensitivity.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations using cost-sensitive and fairness objectives, plus explicit discussion of applicability, feature preparation, multiclass/multiway extrapolation, and caution for oblique trees. It removes the earlier recommendation for additionally regularized objectives on small noisy datasets and the question-length qualification of interpretability. Appendix E newly explains the conflicting mean-accuracy and average-rank ordering.

D1.justification: v2 promises experiment code upon publication; v3 supplies an experiment-repository link and specifies STreeD v1.4.0. It adds CART implementation and clustered hyperparameter-grid details, ConTree’s time limit and timeout list, and revised hardware/memory information: Xeon E5-6248R with 100GB in v2 versus Xeon Gold 6448Y with at most 4GB in v3.

R1.justification: v3 substantially contracts the broad survey of historical methods, alternative heuristics, and ODT applications, including removal of the Noel loss-function discussion and Rashomon, survival, and robustness references. New references such as Blanc et al. (2023), Liu (2022), Ordyniak and Szeider (2021), and cost-sensitive/fairness studies support the revised positioning. The principal previous CART–ODT comparisons remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Three largely self-contained investigations become a shared experimental setup organized around five open questions, preceded by background and comparison practices. Practical recommendations gain a dedicated section, and substantial material moves between the main text and reorganized appendices.

P2.justification: The wider TMLR layout accompanies substantial display changes: v2 Figures 4–5 are combined into v3 Figure 3, the dataset histogram moves into the main text, and the concavity illustration moves to Appendix C. v3 adds a tree illustration, algorithm displays, numerical-feature and balanced-accuracy figures, and a tree-size rank diagram, while removing numerous earlier analytical plots.

improvement.justification: v3 improves organization, corrects the Bayesian loss specification, and strengthens reproducibility disclosures. Appendices D–E address v2’s stated gap concerning unbinarized comparisons and test another objective while reporting timeouts and nonsignificant findings. These provide a modest net improvement, tempered by the loss of small-dataset, objective-noise, and question-length evidence that previously supplied useful breadth and qualifications.
